label: copy-phase input z (fed back from original position >= 2)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is z and recall_idx >= 3 (i.e. the z being re-read was original token 2 or later). Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, including on z in the original sequence, and essentially never on any input other than z (o is a tiny exception). At recall_idx 2 it fires weakly and only sometimes, which accounts for most of the lowest-quartile misses. Magnitude is larger later in the copy phase (mass per activation rises with t) and is highest on runs of consecutive z (top examples are zz near the end of the sequence). It does not depend on out_tok, prev_tok, first_tok, or L beyond these positional effects.

issues: Minor: recall_idx is the index of the token being output, so the fed-back z at recall_idx r is original token r-1. That means recall_idx>=3 corresponds to z from original position >=2, which matches the label and explanation. The wording is correct but easy to misread.

Misses (2621 test steps, 0.8% of mass) are almost all weak activations (~0.04-0.11 of max) on z fed back from original position 1 (recall_idx==2). That predicate has precision 0.14 and mass recall 0.008, which matches the claim that recall_idx 2 fires weakly and only sometimes. Widening to recall_idx>=2 drops F1 to 0.89.

False positives (159 test steps) are concentrated on z from original position 2 (recall_idx==3) in longer sequences: precision 0.983 for L>=7 against 1.000 for L<=5. This is a small effect, not a meaningful systematic gap.
The o exception is confirmed as negligible: copy-phase in_tok==o has precision 0.002.

The claim that magnitude rises with t checks out: activation mass per active step goes from about 1.2e-5 at t=9 to about 2.2e-5 at t=17, and it rises the same way with recall_idx. Phase claims are confirmed: there is zero activation in the original and delimiter phases.
